phase: Phase E - Defensive Engineering: Hardened Policy Examples
note: These are generic, reusable hardened control examples illustrating the AWS security principles behind each flaws.cloud level theme. They are written for a sandbox/reference architecture and use placeholder account IDs / ARNs - replace with your own sandbox values before applying, and validate with 'aws accessanalyzer validate-policy' and/or IAM Policy Simulator prior to use.

1_restrictive_s3_bucket_policy.theme: Level 1/2 - public listing and AuthenticatedUsers exposure
hardening_notes: Grants s3:GetObject only, and only under the /public/ prefix - never s3:ListBucket to '*' or to the AuthenticatedUsers group URI.
Explicit Deny on ListBucket ensures no later, broader statement can accidentally reopen bucket enumeration.
Should be paired with account-level S3 Block Public Access unless the bucket is intentionally a public static website.

2_credential_and_secret_handling.theme: Level 3 - secrets committed to Git history
controls: Enforce a pre-commit hook (git-secrets or gitleaks) that blocks commits containing AWS access-key-shaped strings (AKIA... / ASIA...).
Prefer IAM roles and STS AssumeRole over long-lived IAM user access keys wherever a workload can use them.

If a static key is unavoidable, apply an IAM permissions boundary limiting its maximum possible privilege, and set a mandatory rotation policy (e.g. 90 days) enforced by an AWS Config rule (access-keys-rotated).
On any suspected exposure, immediately deactivate the key (aws iam update-access-key --status Inactive) before investigating, then delete and reissue.

hardening_notes: Account/Region-level Block Public Access for Snapshots prevents any future accidental public share, even if an individual snapshot's attribute is misconfigured.
Sharing should always target explicit account IDs, never the 'all' group.

4_ec2_imdsv2_enforcement.theme: Level 5 - SSRF to Instance Metadata Service
cli_hardening: aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --instance-id i-EXAMPLE --http-tokens required --http-put-response-hop-limit 1 --http-endpoint enabled
hardening_notes: HttpTokens=required enforces IMDSv2, which requires a signed PUT request to obtain a session token - a basic SSRF that only performs a GET request (as in the classic Capital One-style pattern) can no longer reach credentials.
HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1 prevents the token-request PUT from being proxied through an extra network hop, further limiting SSRF reach.
This is a defense-in-depth control - it does not replace fixing the underlying SSRF vulnerability in the application/proxy layer.

5_least_privilege_instance_role.theme: Level 5 - overly broad instance role attached alongside IMDS exposure
hardening_notes: Replaces a broad managed policy (e.g. AmazonS3FullAccess or AdministratorAccess) with the single action and resource the application actually needs.
Even if IMDS credentials are stolen despite IMDSv2, the blast radius is limited to read access on one bucket rather than the whole account.

6_scoped_readonly_audit_role.theme: Level 6 - IAM/Lambda/API Gateway permission discovery via an over-scoped audit identity
hardening_notes: A read-oriented 'audit' identity should be scoped with an explicit permissions boundary and, ideally, no additional customer-managed policy attachments beyond a vetted baseline.

Explicitly denying access to function code (GetFunction) and IAM policy document contents (GetPolicyVersion) still allows architecture-level visibility (what exists) without exposing implementation detail or the exact permission set attached to sensitive roles.
Pair with periodic IAM Access Analyzer 'unused access' review of the audit role to catch permission creep over time.
